faq.q: Does cropping lose quality because the preview is smaller than my photo?
faq.a: No. The crop box is drawn on a scaled-down preview so it fits your screen, but the actual crop is computed in the original image's pixels. The tool keeps a full-resolution copy of the decoded image and reads the X/Y/W/H you set against that, so a region cut from a 4000-pixel photo comes out at its true pixel size, not the preview size. The X/Y/W/H boxes always show the real pixel numbers.

faq.q: Which aspect ratios can I lock the box to?
faq.a: Free (any shape), 1:1, 4:3, 3:4, 16:9, 9:16, 3:2 and passport 35×45, plus a custom ratio where you type your own width and height (for example 35:45 or 2:3). When a ratio is locked, resizing a handle keeps that ratio, and typing a width in the pixel boxes recomputes the height automatically so you can't accidentally break the proportions.

faq.q: Will a photo taken on my phone be cropped sideways?
faq.a: No. Phone photos store an EXIF orientation tag instead of rotating the pixels, which makes some tools crop them rotated. This tool decodes the image with createImageBitmap using imageOrientation 'from-image' (falling back to the browser's own orientation handling), so the picture is upright before you crop and the region you select is the region you get.

faq.q: What format and metadata does the cropped file have?
faq.a: You can keep the original format or choose JPG, PNG or WebP, with a quality slider for the lossy formats. Because the crop is re-encoded from a canvas, EXIF and GPS metadata are dropped from the saved file. The output filename reports the exact pixel dimensions of the crop, and nothing is uploaded — the whole operation runs in your browser.
